en: The Mahāyāna Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha for the Nāga King Sāgara.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma, Dharma Master and Subject Shi Hu, who held the rank of Chao San Da Fu and Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard:

At one time, the Buddha was at the site of enlightenment adorned within the palace of the Sāgara Dragon King in the great ocean, together with a great assembly of seven thousand five hundred bhikṣus, as well as bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who had attained great wisdom, all of whom had gathered from the worlds of the ten directions;

furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Brahmā kings, Śakras, and world-protectors, along with devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and others, who also came to gather there.
At that time, the World-Honored One, seeing that the entire great assembly had gathered, addressed the Dragon King Sāgara, saying:
"O Lord of Dragons!
Behold this world; all manner of karmic actions arise from delusion."
Various mental phenomena will bring about various karmic retributions; if one does not understand this, one will be reborn in various realms of existence.
"Lord of Nagas! You should observe these beings in the great ocean, seeing them manifest in the diverse physical forms of various men."
"O Lord of Nagas!
All these various forms and appearances arise from the diverse transformations of the various minds through all wholesome and unwholesome actions of body, speech, and mind;
yet although this mental dharma is called 'form,' it is like a magical illusion, for there is nothing therein to be grasped."
“O Lord of Nāgas!
These forms and characteristics—of all dharmas—are fundamentally unarisen and devoid of a sovereign;
furthermore, they are without self and without obstruction.”
All such various karmas performed and the intrinsic nature of all phenomena are like illusory transformations, inconceivable. "Dragon Lord!

If there is a bodhisattva who knows that all phenomena are without arising, without cessation, without form, and without characteristics, and having known them as they truly are, performs and cultivates all wholesome karmas without any sense of cultivation or action;”
All forms and characteristics, as well as the aggregates, bases, and elements—all phenomena of birth—are entirely unobservable;
once one has attained this vision according to reality, one should further contemplate exquisite forms and characteristics.
"O Lord of Nāgas!
How should one contemplate these exquisite marks and signs?
One should contemplate the physical marks of the Tathāgata."
The body of the Tathāgata is born from hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of merit.
Furthermore, how is such a mark maintained and adorned?
What is reverent faith?
By it one shall obtain such marks as these; furthermore, how does one obtain freedom from old age and death among humans and in the heavens?
And how does one obtain the bodies of hundreds, thousands, and tens of thousands of gods of the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations, up to the body of a Great Brahmā?
This arises from a mind free of distraction, focusing intently on visualizing and gazing upon the most sublime body of the Tathāgata;
one truly understands that all these exquisite and magnificent physical characteristics are obtained through the accumulation of virtuous karma.
“Lord of Nāgas! Just as your palace and all its adornments are born of merit,

so too, from Brahmā, Śakra, and the World Protectors, down to the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans— all their various adornments are born of merit.”
"Lord of Nagas! Furthermore, within this great ocean, there are all manner of sentient beings—some vast and some minute, many dwelling in ugliness;
yet the bodies of them all are transformations produced by various minds."
"O Lord of Nāgas!
For this reason it is said: 'That which is obtained through the actions of body, speech, and mind.
O Lord of Nāgas!"
Such retribution has karma as its cause and karma as its sovereign.
You should cause all sentient beings to give rise to the mind of wisdom; whatever they do and whatever they cultivate, let them follow and learn from wholesome karma;
regarding all false views, let them neither act upon nor dwell within them.

Knowing that such false views are not ultimate, and having understood this, all sentient beings shall seek him as their teacher and come to provide offerings; furthermore, they shall receive the trust and offerings of both gods and humans.
“Nāgarāja! There is one dharma that can cause sentient beings to sever all karma leading to the evil realms.
What is this one dharma?
This refers to the observation of wholesome dharmas.
How, then, are those wholesome dharmas to be observed?
One should observe one's own body.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down day or night, there is no mental activity I initiate that is not faulty.
Observing in this way, I ensure that no unwholesome states arise within the four modes of deportment.
In this way, having completely eliminated all unwholesome dharmas, one shall cause wholesome dharmas to be fully perfected.

Furthermore, one shall cause all sentient beings who share in these virtues to attain the stages of śrāvaka, pratyekabuddha, and bodhisattva, up to and including the state of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“O Lord of Nāgas!
What are the wholesome dharmas?
I shall now explain them to you.”
What are called the ten wholesome karmas constitute the fundamental basis for all things;
they are the fundamental basis for birth in the heavens and the human realm;
and they are the fundamental basis for the superior wholesome dharmas of both the mundane and supramundane worlds.
It is the fundamental abiding of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas;
it is the fundamental abiding of unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
What constitutes that fundamental abiding?
What are called the ten paths of wholesome action (*daśa-kuśala-karmapatha*).

If one can distance oneself from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, false speech, frivolous speech, harsh speech, and double-tongued speech, and even from covetousness, malice, and wrong views—if one can thus distance oneself from these, this constitutes the ten paths of wholesome action;
they are the fundamental basis for abiding in both the mundane and supramundane realms.
“Lord of Nāgas!
When a person or individual abstains from taking life, they attain ten kinds of wholesome qualities.
What are these ten qualities?
That is to say: attaining the gift of fearlessness;
causing all other sentient beings to abide in a mind of loving-kindness;
attaining right conduct; and attaining the state of not giving rise to thoughts regarding the faults of any sentient being.
One will have few ailments;
one will joyfully obtain a long life;
and various non-human beings will provide protection.
Whether sleeping or awake, they are entirely at peace;
furthermore, they receive the protection of the noble ones, whose minds never weary of them or abandon them;
and within their dreams, they do not see the miseries of evil karma.
One will personally attain fearlessness regarding all evil destinies;
after the end of one's life, one will be reborn in the heavens.
O Lord of Nāgas!
A person or individual who attains these ten kinds of wholesome dharmas and practices the bodhisattva path will achieve abiding in a virtuous mind;
with their roots of goodness matured, they shall attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Lord of Nāgas!
A person, a *pudgala*, who abstains from stealing attains ten supporting qualities. What are these ten?
That is to say: one attains great wealth and sovereignty; one is spared from the perils of kings; one is spared from the calamities of water, fire, thieves, and enemies;
one gains many kinsmen who are virtuous, compliant, and harmonious;
one becomes beloved by many people who do not cause one distress; and whatever one says is received with sincere faith by all.
They shall obtain immeasurable wealth and treasures, all gathered together;
they shall receive universal praise from this world and all other worlds;
and they shall be without fear or dread in any place of activity.
One gains a reputation for being virtuous and is praised for one's wisdom;
furthermore, one attains physical beauty, strength, longevity, and eloquence.
Toward both kin and strangers, the mind remains free from discrimination, never giving rise to affliction or harm.
After the end of his life, he will be reborn in the celestial realms. "Lord of Nāgas!
A person, a *pudgala*, who abstains from stealing attains these ten supporting qualities."
By means of those roots of goodness, one will be able to personally realize and know the qualities of all Buddhas, and shall attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment. "Lord of Nāgas!
A man, a person, who abstains from sexual misconduct attains four wholesome dharmas of wisdom."
What are the four? They are:
subduing the sense faculties;
and remaining free from distraction.
One shall receive all the praises of the world;
furthermore, one shall obtain an immeasurable retinue. "Lord of Nagas!
A person or individual who abstains from sexual misconduct attains these four kinds of wholesome dharmas and wisdom;
by means of these roots of goodness, they shall attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment,
and further realize the mark of a Great Man characterized by the concealment of the male organ.
“Lord of Nāgas!
A person, a *pudgala*, who abstains from false speech attains eight wholesome qualities among gods and humans.
What are these eight?
That is to say, one attains purity of the mouth, which is always like the fragrance of a blue lotus;
furthermore, one attains all correct views in the world,
and attains all that is cherished and delightful in the heavens and among humans.
They attain purity of body, speech, and mind, transforming all sentient beings and causing them to abide in the practice of purity regarding the three karmas;
having attained such purity, all rejoice;
they attain truthful speech, such that their words are invariably sincere and trustworthy.
He has attained superhuman eloquence, and all the words he utters are endowed with skillful means;
among gods and humans, he is free from all faults.
O Lord of Nagas!
A person or individual who abstains from false speech attains these eight kinds of wholesome qualities in the heavens and among humans;
through those roots of goodness, they attain purity of verbal action and practice of truthfulness, and shall eventually attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
“Lord of Nāgas!
A man, a person, who abstains from frivolous speech shall obtain three kinds of exclusively certain dharmas.
What are these three?
What is called "knowing the Dharma" means to always delight in it;
to attain that which is exclusively true and thereby give rise to wisdom; and to become a teacher of humans and devas exclusively, such that all in the heavens and among humans believe and rejoice.
"Lord of Nāgas!
A person, a *pudgala*, who abstains from frivolous speech attains these three kinds of one-pointed dharmas;
by dedicating these roots of goodness toward enlightenment, they receive the prophecy of all Tathāgatas that they shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening."
“Lord of Nāgas!
When a person or individual abandons harsh speech, they attain eight kinds of purity regarding verbal transgressions and acquire eight kinds of wholesome qualities.”
What are the eight? They are:
truthful speech, affectionate speech, speech based on the meaning, gentle speech, speech free from grasping, speech beloved by many, virtuous speech, and speech that is meaningful and beneficial.
"O Lord of Nāgas!
When a person or individual remains far removed from harsh speech, they attain these eight kinds of pure vocal karma.
By dedicating these roots of goodness toward enlightenment, they shall in the future realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, and further obtain the most supreme and pure Brahma-voice."
“Lord of Nagas!
When a person or individual abstains from divisive speech, they shall attain five kinds of firmness.
What are these five kinds of firmness?
That is to say: one attains the firmness of the body, because one shall be far removed from all perils of fear;
one attains the firmness of retinue, because one will not be coveted by others;
one attains the firmness of faith, because one obtains conviction in the retribution of karmic actions.
They attain firmness in the Dharma, because they have attained the stability of the realization of the fruit;
they attain firmness in spiritual friends, because they are always sustained by their affectionate speech.
O Lord of Nāgas!
A person or individual who abstains from divisive speech attains these five kinds of firmness;
by dedicating those roots of goodness toward enlightenment, they shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening,
so that all those such as externalists and Māras may be unable to destroy them.
“Lord of Nāgas!
When a person or individual remains far removed from the poison of greed, they attain eight kinds of wholesome qualities.
What are these eight?

That is to say: attaining the elimination of a greedy mind; attaining the non-arising of a murderous mind; attaining the non-arising of a jealous mind; attaining birth in a noble lineage, with a mind revered by sages;
attaining a mind of loving-kindness, benefiting all sentient beings through wholesome karma;
and attaining physical excellence.
One gains the respect of many people;
one is reborn in the Brahma world,
O Lord of Nagas!
A person, a *pudgala*, having distanced themselves from the poison of greed, attains these eight kinds of wholesome dharmas;
by dedicating these wholesome dharmas toward enlightenment (*bodhi*), their mind does not regress, and they shall realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
“Lord of Nāgas!
A person, a *pudgala*, who remains far removed from the poison of hatred shall attain the fulfillment of five kinds of supreme vows.
What are these five?
That is to say: by not regressing in the cultivation of body, speech, and mind, and by keeping the sense faculties undisturbed, one shall attain the perfection of all vast wealth and nobility;
one shall attain the subjugation of enemies and the perfection of all vast merit and virtue;
and one shall attain the supreme offerings of devas and humans and the perfection of all vast spiritual qualities.
Regarding the most excellent enjoyments and whatever the mind desires, all shall be perfectly fulfilled;
just as when one seeks wealth and status, by making hundreds of thousands of supreme and sublime vows, they are fulfilled according to one's wishes.
"O Lord of Nāgas!
A person or individual who remains free from the poison of hatred attains these five kinds of perfection.
By dedicating these roots of goodness toward enlightenment, they realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening, thereby becoming honored by the three realms."
“Lord of Nāgas!
A person, a *pudgala*, who remains far removed from wrong views attains ten kinds of meritorious qualities.
What are these ten?
That is to say: attaining peace of mind for oneself and having virtuous companions who practice together;
having deep faith in cause and effect, so as not to commit sinful deeds for the sake of body or life;
and before long, attaining the rank of a noble sage.
They attain non-delusion regarding wholesome dharmas and cultivate the conduct of humans and devas;
they do not fall into the realms of animals or Yama;
they practice the noble path and obtain the supreme merit.
One attains liberation from all false dharmas; one attains liberation from the view of a self-body (satkāyadṛṣṭi);
and one attains the vision that the nature of all transgressions is entirely empty.
Having attained [rebirth] among gods and humans, one’s right conduct remains unimpaired.
Lord of Nagas!
A person, a *pudgala*, who is free from wrong views obtains these ten kinds of merit.
“By dedicating these roots of goodness toward enlightenment, one will swiftly be able to realize all Buddha-dharmas and shall attain unsurpassed, perfect, and complete awakening.
‘O Lord of Nāgas!’”
Furthermore, observe that even subtle acts among the ten unwholesome paths of action mostly lead to rebirth in the realms of hell-beings, hungry ghosts, and animals.
"Lord of Nagas!

Observe those sentient beings: if they further take life, they shall fall into the realms of hell, animals, or Yama, and later, when reborn among humans, they will receive two kinds of retribution due to their residual karma:
first, a short lifespan; second, suffering and affliction.

"Furthermore, if one commits theft, they shall fall into the realms of hell, animals, or Yama, and later, upon being born as a human, due to residual karma, they will receive two kinds of retribution:
first, they will dwell in poverty and lowliness; second, they will not obtain the wealth and treasures of others."

"If one further engages in perverse defilement, one shall fall into the realms of hell, animals, or the realm of Yama; subsequently, being born among humans due to residual karma, one will receive two kinds of retribution:
first, stupidity; second, a wife who is not chaste."

"If one further speaks falsely, one shall fall into the hells, the realm of animals, and the world of Yama; later, when reborn among humans, due to residual karma, one will receive two kinds of retribution:
first, one's speech will not be sincere; second, people will not place their trust in one."

"Furthermore, if one engages in frivolous speech, one shall fall into the hells, the animal realm, or the realm of Yama; later, when reborn among humans, due to the remaining karma, one receives two kinds of retribution:
first, one's speech is not truthful; second, what one says lacks consistency."

"Furthermore, if one engages in harsh speech, one shall fall into the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of Yama; later, when reborn as a human due to residual karma, one will receive two kinds of retribution:
first, one's speech will frequently provoke strife and contention; second, people who hear what one says will not hold it in high regard."

"Furthermore, if one engages in divisive speech, one shall fall into the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of Yama; later, when reborn among humans, due to residual karma, one receives two kinds of retribution:
first, one obtains inferior kinsmen; second, one experiences separation from one's relatives."

"If one is further characterized by excessive greed, they shall fall into the realms of hell, animals, or the realm of Yama; subsequently, when reborn as a human, due to residual karma, they will receive two kinds of retribution:
first, being unable to benefit others; second, being constantly harmed by others."

"Furthermore, if one is excessively prone to anger, one shall fall into the realms of hell, animals, or the world of Yama; later, when reborn as a human, due to residual karma, one will receive two kinds of retribution:
first, the mind is constantly unhappy; second, much is contrary to one's wishes."

"Furthermore, those with wrong views shall fall into the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of Yama; later, when reborn as humans, due to residual karma, they will receive two kinds of retribution:
first, wrong views, and second, indolence."
“Nāgarāja! If one practices these ten unwholesome dharmas, one will certainly obtain such retribution, and furthermore, one will separately encounter boundless aggregates of great suffering.”

“Nāgarāja! Furthermore, if a bodhisattva stays far removed from taking life, cultivates the bodhisattva path, and practices giving, they will attain great wealth, long life, and immeasurable merit, and will be freed from all fear of being harmed by others.”
“Lord of Nagas! Furthermore, if a bodhisattva remains far removed from stealing while cultivating the bodhisattva path and practicing generosity, they will attain great wealth and immeasurable merit;
moreover, with a heart free from stinginess toward all things, they will realize profound wisdom and the unsurpassed meaning of the Dharma taught by the Buddhas.”

“Lord of Nāgas! Furthermore, if a bodhisattva remains far removed from perverse attachments, cultivates the bodhisattva path, and practices generosity, he will attain great wealth and status and acquire immeasurable merit;
he will attract virtuous kinsmen, parents, wife, and sons, all of whom will be entirely free from evil views.”
“Lord of Nāgas! Furthermore,
if a bodhisattva stays far removed from false speech while practicing the bodhisattva path and engaging in giving, they will attain great wealth and nobility, acquire immeasurable merit,
and cause all their speech to be entirely virtuous and gentle.”
In all the sincere vows one raises, they shall be firm and steadfast, never regressing. "Lord of Nagas!
Furthermore, if a bodhisattva remains far removed from frivolous speech, cultivates the bodhisattva path, and practices generosity."
One shall attain great wealth and nobility, and acquire immeasurable merit;
one's words will be truthful, such that all who hear them will believe and accept them;
and whatever one says will sever all doubts.
“Lord of Nāgas! Furthermore,
if a bodhisattva remains far removed from harsh speech while cultivating the bodhisattva path and practicing generosity, they will attain great wealth and status, acquire immeasurable merit,
their words will be worthy of acceptance, and no one will turn away upon hearing them.”
Among all assemblies, he is without fault.

"Lord of Nāgas, if a bodhisattva further distances himself from divisive speech while practicing the bodhisattva path and engaging in giving, he will attain great wealth and status and acquire immeasurable merit;
toward his retinue, his mind will abide in equanimity, loving them as one and without causing any separation."
“Lord of Nāgas! Furthermore,
if a bodhisattva remains far removed from the poison of greed, cultivates the bodhisattva path, and practices generosity, they will attain great wealth and status,
acquire immeasurable merit, obtain a handsome body, and possess all sense faculties in full.”
Those who see him love and delight in him, their hearts never wearying of him or turning away from him.

"Lord of Nagas, furthermore, if a bodhisattva remains far removed from the poison of anger while cultivating the bodhisattva path and practicing generosity, he will attain great wealth and nobility and acquire immeasurable merit;
even when encountering enemies, no hostile thoughts will arise in his mind."
Having heard the essentials of the Buddha-dharma, one is able to give rise to deep faith.
"O Lord of Nāgas!
Furthermore, if a bodhisattva remains far removed from false views, cultivates the bodhisattva path, and practices generosity."
One shall attain great wealth and honor, obtain immeasurable merit;
possess right view toward the Triple Gem;
and constantly draw near to the Buddha to hear the sublime Dharma.
He constantly makes offerings to the Sangha without ever becoming weary or regressing;
he teaches and transforms sentient beings, causing them to resolve upon Bodhicitta.
"O Lord of Nagas!

If one can cultivate these ten wholesome deeds and practice the bodhisattva path, first adorning oneself with generosity, one will attain a perfect fruition of reward and achieve great wealth and nobility.
"If one takes upholding the precepts as an adornment, the retribution will be perfected, one will attain all Buddha-dharmas, and one's vows will be fulfilled and complete.

If one takes patience as an adornment, the retribution will be perfected; one will attain the Buddha’s bodhi, the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics, and further obtain the perfection of the Brahma-voice."

"If one uses diligence as adornment, the fruit of retribution will be perfected, and one shall be able to subdue the heavenly Māras and external paths, delivering them through the teachings of all Buddhas."
“If one uses meditative concentration as an adornment, when the fruit of retribution is perfected, one shall attain right mindfulness, purity, and the fulfillment of the practice of Dharma.
If one uses wisdom as an adornment, when the fruit of retribution is perfected, one shall forever sever all false views.”
"If one is adorned with great compassion, the fruit of retribution will be perfected, enabling all sentient beings to subdue all subtle afflictions."
"If one is adorned with great compassion, when its fruit is perfected, one shall attain a state where the minds of all sentient beings never grow weary of or abandon them.
If one is adorned with great joy, when its fruit is perfected, one shall attain a single-mindedness free from distraction."
“If one uses great equanimity as an adornment, the fruit of retribution will be perfected, and one shall attain the complete eradication of even the most subtle afflictions.
O Lord of Nāgas!

"Furthermore, by adorning oneself with the four means of integration (*saṃgrahavastu*), one’s fruition will be perfected, and one shall be able to guide and transform all sentient beings in accordance with their needs.
If one adorns oneself with the four foundations of mindfulness (*smṛtyupasthāna*), one will be able to fully comprehend and understand the body, feelings, mind, and phenomena."
"If one uses the four right efforts as adornments, one can cause all unwholesome dharmas to be completely severed and extinguished, and attain the perfection of all wholesome dharmas."
"If one uses the four bases of psychic power as adornment, one will be able to attain lightness and agility in both body and mind.

If one uses the five faculties as adornment, one shall attain faith and progress without regression, a mind free from delusion, a clear understanding of the causes of all karma, and the eternal extinction of afflictions."
"If one is adorned with the five powers, one shall become neither ignorant nor deluded, and shall attain the permanent severance of the fault of poverty.
If one is adorned with the seven factors of enlightenment, one shall attain the awakening to all dharmas as they truly are."
"If one adorns oneself with the Eightfold Noble Path, one shall be able to realize right knowledge.
If one adorns oneself with śamatha, one shall attain the severance of all afflictions."
"If one is adorned with the *vairambha* wind, one shall attain the wisdom that realizes all phenomena.
If one is adorned with the right path, one shall be able to fully comprehend all skillful means regarding both the conditioned and the unconditioned."
“Lord of Nāgas!

I have now briefly explained the ten wholesome dharmas with their adornments; as for the ten powers, the four kinds of knowledge, the eighteen unique qualities, and even all the categories of the Tathāgata’s dharmas, they are all fully perfected.”
“O Lord of Nagas!
One should cause others to study and practice these ten paths of wholesome action, even at great length, as they constitute the adornment of one’s life.
O Lord of Nagas!”
For example, just as the great earth provides a stable foundation for all the kingdoms, cities, villages, forests, trees, medicinal herbs, and so forth within the human realm;
and furthermore, just as all karmas possess seeds, and these seeds are composed of the four great elements;
and just as when grain is sown, from the initial sprouting of the shoot and stem until its full maturation, it all depends upon the earth.
"O Lord of Nāgas!
These ten paths of wholesome action can provide a supreme and wondrous abode for all sentient beings in the heavens and among humans;
they can cause all conditioned and unconditioned phenomena to attain the fruit of wisdom."
It is that in which all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, up to and including bodhisattvas and unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment, abide;
it is also that in which the root of all Buddha-dharmas abides.
“O Nāga King! All of you should, with upright minds, give rise to faith and understanding regarding what I have here spoken.

At that time, the Nāga King Sāgara, along with all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the assembly, as well as the entire multitude of śrāvakas, devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha for the Nāga King Sāgara.
